solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drunk heads for bits of a ploughman’s lunch? (7,6)

blocks.note: onion is old slang for a head, as in 'off your onion'

annotation.surface: A bleary-eyed crowd of drinkers at the pub, pictured as parts of a plate of food.
annotation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub plate of bread, cheese and pickles. Read 'drunk heads' as two slang words and the pub food falls out.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the question mark flags that pickled onions are one typical item on the plate.

entries.clue: Ridicule international body brought in to prod blubber (4,3,2)

indicatorNotes.brought in to: something brought in to a thing ends up inside it, so the international body goes into the word for blubber

annotation.surface: A mocking instruction to bring a world organisation along to jab at someone overweight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' can also mean to cry, which suits a scene of ridicule, but here it is a noun for whale fat.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain idiom: to poke fun at someone is to mock them, a phrase-for-word synonym of ridicule.

entries.clue: Baptismal robe is bedecked in a lot of shiny metal (7)

indicatorNotes.bedecked in: someone bedecked in finery is wrapped in it, so IS is wrapped in the metal
indicatorNotes.a lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the metal loses its last letter

blocks.note: CHROME, the shiny plating metal, minus its final E

annotation.surface: A christening gown so decorated it seems to be plated in chrome.
annotation.walkthrough: The chrisom is a rare old word, so the wordplay does most of the work here.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, if an old one: the chrisom was the white cloth put on a child at baptism.

entries.clue: Left university deliberately avoiding Conservative with delightful style (10)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to keep it out, so the word for deliberately keeps CON out

blocks.note: CONSCIOUSLY without CON, the short form of Conservative

annotation.surface: Someone who quit college on purpose, steering clear of the Tories, and did it with flair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left university' reads as dropping out, but it is just two abbreviations. CON is the usual short form for a British Conservative.
annotation.definitionFit: Phrase for adverb: luscious means richly delightful, so doing something lusciously is doing it with delightful style.

entries.clue: Please perform, giving medication (6)

blocks.note: the polite 'do', as in 'do come in'

annotation.surface: An audience begging a singer to perform, as if the song were a dose of medicine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Please perform' is a polite request: 'Do sing!'
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to dose a patient is to give them a measured amount of medicine.

entries.clue: Startled once Callas is reviving earlier style (12)

indicatorNotes.Startled: startled creatures scatter in all directions, and so do these letters

annotation.surface: Maria Callas, once jumpy, performing in a revived older fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: Maria Callas was the great opera soprano, which pulls the eye toward music; the answer is an art and architecture term.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: neoclassical art deliberately revives the style of ancient Greece and Rome.

entries.clue: Certain to discard spades, following evident opening (8)

indicatorNotes.to discard: a card player discards by throwing a card away, so SURE throws away S, the bridge abbreviation for spades
indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so the shortened SURE goes after OVERT

annotation.surface: A card player confidently throwing away spades after an obvious lead.
annotation.walkthrough: The card-table surface makes 'opening' look like an opening lead; it is a musical opening.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an overture is the opening piece of an opera, and also an opening approach to someone.

entries.clue: Classify choice of terminus in Southport? (4)

indicatorNotes.terminus in: a terminus is the end of a line, so either end letter of Southport will do

blocks.note: a choice is this or that
last letter of Southport, its other terminus

annotation.surface: Deciding which station to end the journey at in Southport, a seaside town in north-west England.
annotation.walkthrough: A choice between the two ends of Southport is literally 'S or T'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to sort things is to put them into classes.

entries.clue: Story about debt documents displaying wisdom (9)

blocks.note: IOUs are notes acknowledging a debt

annotation.surface: A tale about unpaid IOUs that shows real wisdom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is c. for circa here, not an instruction to put one piece around another.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a sagacious person shows sound judgement, which is wisdom on display.

entries.clue: Oxford University’s skipping redundant source of data relating to helium? (10)

indicatorNotes.skipping: to skip something is to leave it out, so the word for redundant leaves out OU'S

blocks.note: an ID, identification, is where your personal data comes from

annotation.surface: Oxford University passing over a useless pile of information.
annotation.walkthrough: Cooled near absolute zero, liquid helium becomes a superfluid that flows with no friction; the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: helium is the best-known substance that turns superfluid, so the state is tied to it.

entries.clue: Apparently half-cut, rolling over after good Italian spirit (6)

indicatorNotes.half-cut: cut in half, so only the first half of apparently is kept
indicatorNotes.rolling over: something that rolls over ends up the other way round, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.after: the reversed piece comes after G

blocks.note: the first five letters of APPARENTLY's ten

annotation.surface: Someone seemingly tipsy and falling over after a glass of good Italian spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, which fits the spirit, but here it halves the word 'apparently'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain example: grappa is the Italian brandy distilled from grape pressings.

entries.clue: Obsessive person using computer means to find rest, after first escapes (7,5)

indicatorNotes.after first escapes: once its first letter has escaped, the word for rest is left without it

blocks.note: Control-F is the keyboard shortcut to find text
BREAK, a rest, without its first letter B

annotation.surface: Someone fixated on their computer, hunting for a way to relax.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Computer means to find' is the Ctrl+F shortcut spelled out.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a control freak is obsessed with controlling everything around them.

entries.clue: Operating system with alternative name of Japanese city (5)

blocks.note: the first letters of Operating System

annotation.surface: Computer software given a different name, like a city renamed.
annotation.walkthrough: The computing surface hides a place name; 'with' and 'of' only join the parts to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Osaka is one of Japan's largest cities.

entries.clue: Wildly spends the last of gift, say, when the sales start? (2,8,3)

indicatorNotes.Wildly: letters used wildly go all over the place, out of order
indicatorNotes.the last of: the last of something is its final part, here gift's final letter

annotation.surface: A shopper blowing money wildly once the post-Christmas sales begin.
annotation.walkthrough: St Stephen's Day is 26 December, Boxing Day in Britain, when the big post-Christmas sales traditionally open.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic by example: the post-Christmas sales traditionally open on 26 December, which is this saint's feast day.

entries.clue: Edges back before rather dumb suburbs, last places to be seen (5)

indicatorNotes.last places to be seen: the last place in each word is where the letter to be seen is

annotation.surface: Backing along the edges of a dull suburb, the last spots anyone visits.
annotation.walkthrough: Kerb is the British spelling of curb, the raised edge of a pavement.
annotation.definitionFit: Specific for general: kerbs are the edges of pavements and roads.

entries.clue: Succulent plant one starts to cultivate regularly, in conclusion (9)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of words are their first letters
indicatorNotes.in: the pieces before it go in the word for conclusion

annotation.surface: Gardening advice: grow this succulent regularly and you will get there in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but it is just a word whose first letter is needed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: stonecrop is a sedum, a low-growing succulent.

entries.clue: Toughens former monarch as well? Nearly (7)

indicatorNotes.Nearly: a word nearly given stops just short, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: Does a queen of old strengthen things too? More or less.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' is split off by the question mark, but it still acts on the words just before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical synonym: annealing metal or glass by heating and slow cooling makes it tougher.

entries.clue: Classy dresser represented — alas — in the fop (7,5)

indicatorNotes.represented: re-presented, set out again, here in a new order

annotation.surface: A sigh that a stylish dresser is being played as a dandy.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder even describes the answer: a fop is a vain dresser.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a fashion plate, from the illustrations in old fashion magazines, is someone always stylishly dressed.

entries.clue: Respectable reputation — it’s led by significant character? (6,4)

blocks.note: a good name is a good reputation

annotation.surface: A good reputation, won by someone of important character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Significant character' sounds like an important person, but it is a capital letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a proper name always begins with a capital, a character that signifies something.

entries.clue: Student group storing one megabit in the cloud (6)

indicatorNotes.storing: whatever stores something keeps it inside, so the student group holds the other letters

blocks.note: the National Union of Students, the UK student body

annotation.surface: Students keeping their data in cloud storage.
annotation.walkthrough: The computing 'cloud' is a false trail; the answer is a real rain cloud.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a nimbus is a rain cloud.

entries.clue: Small example of plagiarism almost ruined careless writing (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word, so it stops one letter short

blocks.note: to crib is to copy someone's work
BLEW (as in 'blew it') without its last letter

annotation.surface: A bit of copying that nearly spoiled a sloppy essay.
annotation.walkthrough: A crib is a student's word for copied work; 'blew it' means ruined it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a scribble is writing dashed off without care.

entries.clue: Deception in wager? Wager Arab brought up (8)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, bringing letters up makes them read from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: to lay money is to wager it
a dictionary abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

annotation.surface: A bettor cheated after laying money on an Arab racehorse.
annotation.walkthrough: The two 'wager' words give different synonyms, and only the second one turns upward with the Arab.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a betrayal deceives someone who trusted you.

entries.clue: Make white line in sand? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the line is put in the sand, inside the word for it

blocks.note: a beach is a stretch of sand

annotation.surface: Drawing a white line in the sand.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's white line is just paint; 'Make white' at the front is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to bleach something is to whiten it.

entries.clue: A call to block popular sources of historical analysis in unaccepted books (9)

indicatorNotes.to block: something that blocks a passage sits in the middle of it, so the call sits inside the word for popular
indicatorNotes.sources of: a source is where something starts, so take first letters

annotation.surface: Scholars calling for a ban on popular history books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Block' reads as a ban in the surface, but it is an instruction to sit inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the Apocrypha are books left out of the accepted biblical canon.

entries.clue: Son going off job in stables? (8)

blocks.note: eggs addle when they go off

annotation.surface: A son quitting his stable-hand job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going off' looks like leaving, but it means rotting, as eggs addle.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: saddling horses is one routine task in a stable yard.

entries.clue: Coastal region somewhat holding boy back, leading to crime (5,5)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold is to keep inside, so the word for somewhat keeps the boy inside it
indicatorNotes.back: sending it back means reading it backwards
indicatorNotes.leading to: what leads to something comes first, so SIN follows

annotation.surface: A seaside area where keeping a youngster back turns into crime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' applies to the whole package, not just the boy: the container is built first, then reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a tidal basin is a harbour area on the coast where water rises and falls with the tide.

entries.clue: Ambassadors etc stumped up in support of qualification (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, letters sent up read from the bottom, so backwards
indicatorNotes.in support of: a support goes underneath, and in a down clue underneath means after

blocks.note: st. is the scorecard abbreviation for stumped in cricket

annotation.surface: Envoys who paid up to back a qualification.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stumped up' looks like 'paid up', but it is a cricket scorecard abbreviation turned upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Class by example: ambassadors are the best-known kind of diplomat, and 'etc' covers the rest.

entries.clue: Newspaper feature in the immediate future about journey by wagon (5,7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the word for the immediate future goes around the rest
indicatorNotes.by: one thing by another sits beside it, so the wagon sits beside the journey

annotation.surface: A newspaper promising a piece soon about travelling by wagon.
annotation.walkthrough: Strip cartoon is the British name for a comic strip.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a strip cartoon is a regular item in the paper.

entries.clue: Company with problem about Mass — Bach? (8)

blocks.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
a poser is a puzzling problem

annotation.surface: A choir with trouble over a Mass, perhaps one by Bach.
annotation.walkthrough: Bach did write Masses, so the religious sense of Mass is the bait; it is the physics symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: J S Bach is one composer, which the question mark flags.

entries.clue: Press barons ultimately put up with endless acclaim (8)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter
indicatorNotes.endless: without its end, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to hang a picture is to put it up

annotation.surface: Newspaper owners tolerating nothing but applause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press barons' reads as newspaper owners, but Press stands alone as a verb, as in press-gang.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to shanghai someone is to press them into service by force.

entries.clue: Fool screwed up everything? Not entirely (4)

indicatorNotes.Not entirely: what is not entirely there is only partly there, so the answer is part of the words

annotation.surface: An idiot who messed up almost everything.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, which is why 'not entirely' covers the whole phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to dupe someone is to fool them, and a dupe is someone fooled.

entries.clue: Impact on pitch allowing assessment of pace? (7,6)

annotation.definition: Impact on pitch allowing assessment of pace?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a ball landing on a cricket pitch; the setter means a change in the pitch of a sound
the surface pushes judging a bowler's speed; the setter means measuring speed from that shift, as radar guns do

annotation.surface: A bowler's delivery hitting the cricket pitch and revealing how fast it was.
annotation.walkthrough: Pitch and pace suggest cricket, but pitch is the note of a sound: a moving source changes it, which lets speed guns measure pace.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the Doppler effect is a shift in pitch caused by motion, used to measure speed.

entries.clue: Something extremely close that’s cold and warm? (4,4)

annotation.surface: A weather forecast that can't decide between cold and warm.
annotation.walkthrough: Cold and warm look like opposites that cancel out; each is just a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a dead heat is a race finish too close to separate.

entries.clue: I have an opposite number not feeling well? (8)

blocks.note: having an opposite number means being paired

annotation.surface: Someone with a counterpart who is feeling off colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I have an opposite number' is 'I'm paired', which run together spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: impaired means weakened, and the question mark admits the stretch to feeling unwell.

entries.clue: Well-mannered church event for officials (5,7)

annotation.surface: A polite church gathering held for dignitaries.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one event, but the two halves are separate words for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the civil service is the whole body of government officials.

entries.clue: Last eccentric eggs me on to publicise climbing, flowering plant (12)

indicatorNotes.eccentric: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are out of their usual order
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, a climbing word goes up, reading backwards

blocks.note: to air an opinion is to publicise it

annotation.surface: Someone odd egging the writer on to announce a climbing plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eggs me on' reads as encouragement, but eggs is a noun and me is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: alstroemeria, the Peruvian lily, is a flowering plant.

entries.clue: Supporting bestseller, interrupted by current book ban (8)

indicatorNotes.interrupted by: something interrupted has a break in the middle, and the break is filled by the next letters

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for current

annotation.surface: A bestselling book suddenly facing a ban.
annotation.walkthrough: Current here is electrical, not up to date.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to prohibit is to forbid, to ban.

entries.clue: Oil giant in trouble? No relief here (8)

indicatorNotes.in trouble: things in trouble are in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A struggling oil company with no respite in sight.
annotation.walkthrough: Relief here is the carving term: relief stands out from a surface, while intaglio is cut into it.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: intaglio is carved into the surface, so it is the opposite of relief work.

entries.clue: Agile mole crossing river (4)

indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross a river is to span it, so the spy spans the R, one letter each side and more

annotation.surface: A nimble mole paddling across a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The animal is a false trail; a mole is a planted spy.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: spry means lively and nimble.

entries.clue: Statesman energised nation’s men (10)

indicatorNotes.energised: energised things move about, so the letters are stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: A politician who fires up his country's men.
annotation.walkthrough: Statesman looks like a politician, but it is a state's man: someone from the US state of Minnesota.
annotation.definitionFit: Punning definition: read as state's man, it means a man from a US state, and Minnesota is one.

entries.clue: Cast recording in hobbyist’s collection (5,5)

blocks.note: to stamp is to mould or impress a shape, as a cast does

annotation.surface: A cast recording kept among a collector's treasures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast recording' suggests a musical's soundtrack; the words split into two separate synonyms.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a stamp collector keeps the collection in an album.

entries.clue: Star unimportant after opening game’s beginning (7,5)

indicatorNotes.after: what comes after goes later, so the word for unimportant ends the answer
indicatorNotes.beginning: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A star player looking insignificant after the opening of a match.
annotation.walkthrough: The parts are assembled in the reverse of the clue's order.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a leading light is a prominent figure, a star in their field.

entries.clue: Various letters by a politician as source of illumination (10)

indicatorNotes.Various: various means assorted, so the letters come in an assorted order
indicatorNotes.by: one thing by another sits beside it

annotation.surface: An MP whose assorted letters are meant to enlighten.
annotation.walkthrough: The word 'letters' is both what the surface is about and the anagram fodder itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a street lamp is one source of light.

entries.clue: Praise intense emotion about European poem, overlooking opening line (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the pang goes around the E
indicatorNotes.overlooking opening: to overlook is to leave out, so the poem leaves out its opening letter, L for line

blocks.note: a pang is a sharp feeling
LYRIC without its opening L, line

annotation.surface: Admiring a moving European poem while skipping its first line.
annotation.walkthrough: The poem's 'opening line' is its first letter L, which also stands for line.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a panegyric is a speech or poem of lavish praise.

entries.clue: Bottom of the German stream, not very flexible, ultimately (8)

indicatorNotes.not: not very means without V, the abbreviation for very
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter

annotation.surface: The bed of a German river that barely bends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of the German stream' paints a riverbed; Bottom is the backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Euphemism: derrière, French for 'behind', is a polite word for the bottom.

entries.clue: Stop checking island combat (6)

indicatorNotes.checking: to check something is to hold it back, so the word for stop holds the island in

annotation.surface: Halting an invasion of an island by fighting.
annotation.walkthrough: Combat is a verb here, to fight against, not a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to resist is to fight against, to combat.

entries.clue: Soldier essentially gains woman’s love, unsettling protagonist (8)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence is the heart of a thing, so the middle letter of gains

annotation.surface: A soldier winning a woman's heart, a story with a troubling hero.
annotation.walkthrough: The soldier is an insect, not a serviceman.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: an antihero is a protagonist lacking heroic virtues, which unsettles readers.

entries.clue: Criticise one’s joke about golf (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the joke goes around G

blocks.note: one is I, and one's is I'm

annotation.surface: Mocking one's own joke about golf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'I'm', the contraction of 'I am', not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to impugn a claim is to attack it as false, to criticise it.

entries.clue: Components of theatre in links formed at college? (7)

annotation.surface: Parts of a drama made from friendships formed at university.
annotation.walkthrough: The unities are the classical rules of drama: one time, one place, one action.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical sense: the dramatic unities of time, place and action are components of classical theatre.

entries.clue: Space for printer in choice assembly (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the printer's space goes in the word for choice

blocks.note: a plum job is a choice one
an en is a printer's space

annotation.surface: Finding room for a printer in a hand-picked meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of space, half an em.
annotation.definitionFit: Formal synonym: a plenum is a full meeting of all members, an assembly.

entries.clue: Beer initially on house, perhaps, making you drunk (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so B comes first

blocks.note: house, or housey-housey, is the old name for bingo, a lotto game

annotation.surface: Free beer on the house, getting you drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the house' means free, but house is a lotto game: housey-housey is the old British name for bingo.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: blotto is British slang for very drunk.

entries.clue: Writing about confused leader, one supporting American approach? (10)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the writing goes around the rest
indicatorNotes.confused: a confused leader is a muddled one, so the letters of leader are muddled

annotation.surface: A column about a muddled president, written by one of his backers.
annotation.walkthrough: Fist is old slang for handwriting.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the US is a federal union, so a federalist backs that American system.

entries.clue: Short answer in crisis (5)

blocks.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram

annotation.surface: A curt reply given during an emergency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short answer' reads as a curt reply, but a short is a British word for a shot of spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a drama is a tense, exciting situation, which a crisis is.

entries.clue: Announcing Trump going not quite all out (12)

indicatorNotes.not quite: not quite all of a word stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out are out of place, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: A report that Trump is nearly all gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going out' looks like a departure, but out is the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Formal synonym: to promulgate a law is to announce it officially.

entries.clue: Mushy peas for recess (4)

indicatorNotes.Mushy: mushy peas are mashed, so the letters are mashed into a new order

annotation.surface: Mushy peas served at break time.
annotation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British chip-shop side, and recess suggests a school break; it is an alcove.
annotation.definitionFit: Architectural sense: an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church.

entries.clue: Dodging the question recalled response to “Do you spend?” (7)

indicatorNotes.recalled: recalled means called back, so the reply is read backwards

annotation.surface: A thrifty person sidestepping a question about their spending.
annotation.walkthrough: The saver's reply is itself a way of avoiding the question.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: evasion is avoiding giving a straight answer.

entries.clue: Classified “retired” after church position rejected (3-6)

indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is thrown back, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.after: the word for retired comes after the turned piece

annotation.surface: A retired cleric turned down for a church post, all hush-hush.
annotation.walkthrough: Retired sounds like a pensioner, but it is just its abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Grading term: top-secret is the highest level of classified information.

entries.clue: Pipe twisted in inferior Airbnb (5)

indicatorNotes.twisted: twisted round means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A leaking pipe found in a disappointing holiday rental.
annotation.walkthrough: The pipe is for smoking, not plumbing.
annotation.definitionFit: Material for object: pipes carved from briar root are themselves called briars.

entries.clue: Jazz star backed bringing in second skilled performer (9)

indicatorNotes.backed: backed means sent backwards, so the star's word reads in reverse
indicatorNotes.bringing in: whatever brings something in holds it inside, so the reversed star takes S inside

blocks.note: a big name is a star

annotation.surface: A jazz star supported by a talented sideman.
annotation.walkthrough: The music surface makes performer sound like a musician; a tradesman performs skilled manual work.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a tradesman is someone who performs a skilled trade, such as a plumber.

entries.clue: Background stuff, its volume modulated with care (8,5)

indicatorNotes.modulated: a modulated sound has been altered, so the letters are altered in order

annotation.surface: A sound engineer carefully adjusting the volume of some background noise.
annotation.walkthrough: The audio surface fits the answer, which makes 'modulated' easy to miss as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal description: elevator music is the bland recorded music played in the background of lifts and shops.
